claim: written_by_command re-derives the 'this command writes its argument' rule that shell_paths.by_command (shell_paths.py:217-229) already holds, from the same tables and with the same arithmetic — ALWAYS writes every file argument, TO_LAST writes the last one unless -t/--target-directory names the target, IN_PLACE writes when a flag matches `^-[A-Za-z]*i|^--in-place` (the regex is literally repeated at shell_paths.py:228 and shell_readonly.py:152), dd writes `of=` — so a change to which flags mean in-place, or a new command in TO_LAST's handling, has to be made in both modules; the two modules differ only in SKIP_FIRST / sed -e (readonly) and git / awk inplace (paths).

evidence.detail: by_command: u.cmd in ALWAYS -> True; dd -> of=; TO_LAST -> is_last or -t/--target-directory; IN_PLACE -> any(re.match(r"^-[A-Za-z]*i|^--in-place", w))
written_by_command: cmd in sp.ALWAYS -> files; sp.TO_LAST -> --target-directory=/-t value else files[-1:]; sp.IN_PLACE and re.match(r"^-[A-Za-z]*i|^--in-place", w) -> files; dd -> of= values

the module's own docstring states the intent: 'the write rules of shell_paths.py, asked of EVERY path instead of the protected ones' — the redirection, output-flag and inline-call rules are reused through sp.Use/sp.by_output_flag/sp.by_call at lines 167-171; only by_command is re-derived
